correctness.rationale: Ordinary Roman domination requires each zero-labeled vertex adjacent to at least one label two. The graph is a clique C_n, independent matched/co-matched feet S_n, and arbitrary head H of order r joined to all core vertices. For thin spiders, partition labelings by existence of core twos and of head twos. In the core-two class each index contributes X=z²(1+z+z²) if core=2 or D=z(1+z)² if core !=2 and foot >0; exclude the no-core-two case. Head labels then unrestricted, Q^r. In the no-core-two/head-two class the head must be Roman valid with at least one two, giving (R_H-z^r)D^n. In the no-two class head all-one and each matched pair contributes 2z²+z³. This yields Q^r((X+D)^n-D^n)+(R_H-z^r)D^n+z^r(2z²+z³)^n. The thick case core-two class excludes all no-two cores E^n and the n unique-core-two configurations with its unmatched foot zero, nz²E^(n-1); the no-two-core/head-two class is same D term. In no-head/core-two class feet-two count 0,1,>=2 yields exactly K_n=B^n((z+z²)^n-z^n-nz^(n+1))+n z^(n+2) B^(n-1)+z^(2n). Resulting thick formula is Q^r(Q^(2n)-E^n-nz²E^(n-1))+(R_H-z^r)D^n+z^r K_n. Disjoint-label partitions prove full coefficients for all n>=2 and arbitrary H, including empty. Union multiplicativity and join four-class identity were independently checked. Applying established P4-sparse decomposition gives finite recursion. Independent complete coefficient enumeration verified ten n/head/type instances; these tests are finite corroboration.
